beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:curious, a little playful]About eight thousand years ago, people in Tunisia, in North Africa, left behind whole ^hills of snail shells.
[d:tension][act:the twist, intrigued]And the DNA of one of them points to an ancestor from across the ^sea.

[d:calm][act:plain, orienting]Archaeologists call these people the ^Capsians, after ^Capsa, the ancient name of the town of ^Gafsa. [p:0.93][act:steady, explaining]They were foragers: they lived by hunting and gathering, not by ^farming. [act:steady]They ranged over inland Tunisia and ^Algeria, from about eleven thousand to seven and a half thousand years ago.

[d:build][act:vivid, a little amazed]Their camps grew into mounds of ash, burnt stone, tools and ^shells, some more than three metres ^deep: deeper than an ordinary room is ^tall. [p:0.93][gap:0.4][act:counting, amused]At one site, archaeologists counted the ^shells in a single cubic ^metre, a box one metre on each side. [p:0.9][act:the punchline, savouring it]About twenty-five ^thousand. [p:0.93][act:playful, doing the sum]Eat one snail a minute@time, non-stop, and that box alone would take you more than two ^weeks.

[d:aside][act:light, correcting a myth]But snails weren't the ^main meal. [act:matter of fact][tune:fall]The bones in the mounds say ^big game was. [p:0.93][act:explaining, a smile]A snail is one ^mouthful. [act:explaining, plain][tune:fall]One big animal feeds the whole ^camp.

[d:reveal][act:the reveal, leaning in]Then, in {2025|twenty twenty-five}, came ancient ^DNA from a forager buried at ^Djebba, in northwest Tunisia, about seven thousand nine hundred years ago. [p:0.9][act:precise, delighted]Split his ancestry into a hundred ^parts, and almost ^six came from hunter-gatherers of ^Europe. [act:the clue, careful]Probably by way of ^Sicily. [p:0.93][gap:0.4][act:curious, the method]How do we ^know? [act:explaining, clear]DNA can survive in ancient ^bone, and comparing genomes is a bit like spotting a family ^likeness in old photographs.

[d:build][go:1|0][act:connecting it, wonder]And a second clue comes from ^stone. [p:0.93][act:explaining, clear]Obsidian is a dark volcanic ^glass, and every volcano's glass carries its own chemical ^fingerprint, so a blade can be traced back ^home. [act:the payoff, wonder]Obsidian from the island of ^Pantelleria, between Tunisia and Sicily, shows people were already crossing the ^sea.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, even][tune:rise]Stone Age sea contact between Tunisia and ^Sicily? [act:the verdict, measured][tune:fall]^*Plausible*. [act:fair, a caveat]The signal is real, but it comes from ^one person. [p:0.93][act:explaining, fair]One genome is a ^clue, not yet a ^pattern.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:inviting, warm]We need more ^genomes. [act:the last word, a smile][tune:fall]And perhaps a few more ^snails.
